label: heart100-s4
summary: The model (training AUC 0.954) is mostly a linear clinical risk score: the direct terms carry the ranking (switching them off drops the training AUC to 0.506), with more vessels on fluoroscopy, exercise angina, male sex, a flat ST slope and cholesterol raising the score, and a normal thallium scan, typical or non-anginal chest pain and a higher maximum heart rate lowering it. An ST-depression hinge adds risk from 0.5 mm upward, and a weak blood-pressure hinge from 128 mm Hg upward. The main interaction is a protective gate, open for 102 of 242 training patients (96 men, 6 women) and shut for every one of the 33 with high fasting blood sugar (0 open): exercise angina or atypical angina opens it, high blood pressure and heart rate close it, and when open it takes the exercise-angina penalty back off. In the typical man with normal blood sugar, exercise angina moves the predicted risk from 28% to 26%, while in the typical woman it raises it from 1% to 12%; in that man with exercise angina, raising resting blood pressure from 100 mm Hg to 180 mm Hg lifts the risk from 7% to 83%, mostly by closing the gate. Switching the gate off moves the training AUC to 0.920. Against clinical expectation, high fasting blood sugar has a negative direct term (-0.67 per sd) and atypical angina a positive one (0.20 per sd); both features also act through the gate.
